findings.why: Under a headline about irritation, listing "sensitive" skin beside a patch-test line reads as a promise that the serum won't irritate sensitive skin. The page's own FAQ (F33) says people with extra sensitive skin should consult a dermatologist first, and the ad drops that caveat.
findings.fix: Keep the page's suitability wording and add its caveat: "Dry/normal, sensitive, oily/combination, acne-prone skin. Extra-sensitive skin: consult a dermatologist first." Or keep the headline neutral so the line does not read as an irritation reassurance.

tone_read: Calm, practical and educational: it names a worry (irritation) but answers with usage steps, patch-test wording and sunscreen advice instead of agitating. The question-led opener is the one line a brand reviewer might soften.
language_read: "Alpha Arbutin 2%" is in house format and the patch-test line uses the brand's narrower approved wording ("under a Dermatologist's supervision"). The suitability line is the page's own but omits the page's caution for extra-sensitive skin.
